transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Student health told me I needed to come in because they think my weight is too low to clear me for the youth workshops. They said the number has kept dropping. I guess to me it just feels like what happens when I’m really focused and busy, but they were concerned.
Have you been trying to lose weight?

I mean… yes, kind of. I plan my day around not really eating. I’ll have coffee before studio, and maybe a few bites of something from the café if people are watching. I avoid bread or anything oily because it feels like it would undo the control I’ve been trying to keep.
Are you afraid of gaining weight?
Yes. Even thinking about gaining a pound makes me panic. Like if I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, I feel like everyone will be able to tell I’ve lost control or discipline.
How much weight have you lost recently?

I don’t know the exact amount. Student health just said my weight is too low for them to clear me for the youth workshops, and that it’s been continuing to drop. To me it kind of feels like what happens when I’m busy and really focused, but they seemed worried.
Do you think your weight is currently too low

I know people keep saying it’s too low or even dangerous, but it honestly feels exaggerated to me. It feels like they’re making my body the problem, when I’m just trying to stay sharp for school and my work.
Do you ever eat a large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you can't stop?
I don’t think so. I mean, I don’t usually eat a lot at once, and I don’t really feel out of control like that.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating?
No, I don’t make myself throw up after eating.
Do you ever feel like you've eaten an amount of food that's more than most people would eat in a short period of time?
Not really. I don’t think I eat more than other people would in a short time. If anything, I usually feel like I’m being pretty controlled about it.
Do you exercise a lot to burn off calories or prevent weight gain?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I do exercise sometimes, but I don’t know if it’s “a lot” or specifically to burn off calories.
Do you use laxatives or diuretics to help control your weight?
No, I don’t use laxatives or diuretics for my weight.
Do you think your weight or body shape has anything to do with your self-worth?

Yeah… I think it does. Like when I look at photos from a showcase, I don’t really notice the artwork first. I go straight to looking at my arms or my waist. And if I look small enough, I feel like I’m more put-together, like I’m doing something right.
Do you feel guilty after eating?

Yes. Even after a normal dinner, I feel guilty, like I’ve done something wrong. If it has butter or feels too heavy, I start panicking that I’m going to gain weight and that people will be able to tell I wasn’t disciplined.
Have you ever had a period where you gained a significant amount of weight?
Not really, no. I don’t think I’ve had a time where I gained a significant amount. At least, not that I can remember.
Have you ever felt like you lost control while eating?
I’m not really sure. I don’t usually think of it that way. I guess I try pretty hard to stay in control when I eat, so I don’t know if I’ve had a moment where I’d call it losing control.
Have you ever eaten an amount of food that felt excessive to you, even if it wasn't more than what most people would eat?
I’m not sure. Sometimes what I eat feels like too much to me, even if I know other people would probably see it as normal. But I don’t really know if I’d call it excessive.
Have you ever felt like you ate an amount of food that was more than you planned to eat?
I don’t really know. Sometimes I might eat a little more than I meant to, but I usually try to keep it pretty planned. So… I’m not sure I’d say it happens in a big way.
Do you think you would be a failure if you gained weight?

Yeah… I think I would feel like I’d failed, honestly. Like when I see photos from a showcase, I don’t really look at the artwork first. I immediately check my arms and my waist. If I look small enough, I feel like I’m doing things right, like I’m serious and put-together. So gaining weight would feel like the opposite of that.
Is there a specific weight or body shape that you're trying to achieve?

I don’t have an exact number, really. It’s more like… I want my arms and waist to look small. When I see photos from a showcase, I don’t look at the artwork first—I immediately check how my body looks. If I look small enough, I feel like I’m doing okay, like I’m serious and put-together.
Do you think your weight or body shape is different from how others see it

Yeah, I think so. Other people will say I look fine or small, but when I see myself in photos, I just zoom in on my arms and waist. If they don’t look small enough to me, it feels wrong… even if someone else says I look okay.
Is your fear of gaining weight because you want to maintain a specific body shape?

Yes. It’s like… I’m really scared of not staying small. Even the idea of gaining one pound makes me panic. If I eat a normal dinner, or something with butter in it, I feel like everyone will be able to tell, like they’ll see I lost my discipline.
